page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal server belonging to the compute-optimized family, powered by AWS Graviton ARM64 processors. It delivers 192 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Each core hosts a single hardware execution thread without simultaneous multithreading, eliminating resource contention across virtual threads. Operating in a non-virtualized bare-metal configuration, the host grants unmediated direct access to physical CPU and system resources. The server integrates 384 GB of total system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core.

Storage and network resources are provisioned directly on the host hardware. The configuration bundles 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, enabling low-latency and high-throughput local disk I/O. Host network communication is supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. The server does not include discrete GPU accelerators, coprocessors, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of 192 dedicated physical cores and substantial integrated NVMe capacity yields high computational and I/O density on a single node without hypervisor penalties. However, utilization of the arm64 architecture requires application software compiled specifically for ARM, precluding use of x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512. The hardware configuration aligns with CPU-bound and I/O-intensive workloads, including distributed database nodes, high-throughput data processing, large-scale CI/CD build farms, and batch computation.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture using AWS Graviton processors. The machine supplies 192 physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core and no hypervisor overhead. System memory totals 384 GB, providing a standard compute-optimized memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary storage, the server integrates 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity directly on the host. Network connectivity is delivered via a 100 Gbps baseline interface, and the system contains zero GPU accelerators. Because the machine relies on dedicated arm64 hardware, workloads must target ARM binaries rather than x86 instruction sets. The high core count combined with substantial high-throughput local disk storage renders the platform suitable for multi-threaded compute workloads, large-scale distributed analytics, high-IOPS data processing, and batch compute pipelines.
